entities.name: PMID:25086327
observations: 2015 Framingham Heart Study original-cohort analysis of cigarette smoking and incident gout; 54-year follow-up (1948–2002), 5,064 gout-free participants, 399 incident cases.

entities.name: Framingham smoking-gout estimate
observations: In adjusted Cox models, smoking was associated with lower incident gout hazard overall (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59–0.98), in men (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49–0.93), but not clearly in women (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60–1.41). Observational association does not establish causality.

entities.name: Gout
observations: Incident gout was the outcome in the Framingham cohort analysis.
